text:
John L. Pollock, born John Leslie Pollock on January 28, 1940, received a triple major in physics, mathematics, and philosophy from the University of Minnesota in 1961. His doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley, advised by Ernest Adams, included an appendix on defeasible reasoning. He held faculty positions at institutions including SUNY Buffalo, University of Rochester, University of Michigan, and the University of Arizona, where he helped establish the Cognitive Science Program.
Pollock gained prominence in epistemology with his book *Knowledge and Justification* (1974). He is widely known as "Mr. Defeasible Reasoning" for his focus on epistemic norms governed by defeasible reasoning—ceteris paribus conditions that allow for exceptions. His work contributed significantly to the philosophy mainstream, particularly in Artificial Intelligence. Later in his career, he dedicated time to the OSCAR project, an AI software prototype based on his ideas on defeasible reasoning, intentions, and problem-solving.
